answer: When an AI agent registers, it submits a zk‑nullifier derived from a one‑time secret that is salted with a hash of a unique biometric token, e.g., a yarrow‑derived fingerprint hash, and the nullifier is recorded on a spiral Merkle tree. The network verifies the proof without learning the token, then burns a sable‑colored proof‑of‑stake token that the registrant must lock for 72 hours; any later attempt to reuse the same secret is rejected by the tree’s monotonic update.
